summary.headline: Dodla Dairy Q1 FY27 revenue hit record INR1,198 crore (+19% YoY) but EBITDA margin fell to 5.4% from 8.2% on procurement costs; management guides 7-8% margin recovery.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue reached a record INR1,198 crore, up 19% YoY, with milk procurement at 21.1 lakh litres per day (+13% YoY). EBITDA was INR65 crore (5.4% margin) and PAT INR41 crore, as procurement prices stayed elevated (INR41.3/litre vs INR37.4 a year ago) and price pass-through lagged. Management says the pressure is seasonal rather than structural, and it has since taken a further milk price correction of around 2-2.5% in the ongoing quarter. Africa and VAP delivered strong growth, while Orgafeed margins were under pressure.

financial_highlights.change: YoY decline; no tax credit this quarter vs prior quarters
+18% YoY (OSAM addition, new minimum wage rules)

financial_highlights.value: INR158 crore (corrected from 159 crore on call)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR352.8 crore YoY; highest ever

segments.name: Dodla India (standalone)
segments.commentary: Milk procurement 17.23 lakh litres/day (+3% YoY); milk sales 13.6 lakh litres/day (+14.5%); average milk realisation INR59.4/litre vs INR57.2 YoY, against procurement cost INR41.3/litre. Standalone milk revenue grew about 4.9% YoY; curd and curd products grew about 41% YoY.

segments.name: Africa (Kenya and Uganda)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR154 crore (+45.6% YoY), EBITDA INR24 crore (+74%); blended realisation about INR65/litre vs about INR59-61 a year ago. Kenya capacity about 80% utilised (1.5 lakh litre installed); Uganda described as at full capacity, with a greenfield plan being considered. Market share about 50% in Uganda long-life milk and yogurt, 2-3% in Kenya.

segments.name: OSAM Dairy
segments.commentary: Revenue INR91 crore in the quarter; management says procurement now roughly matches sales after avoiding powder and butter purchases, and profitability is gradually improving.

segments.name: Orgafeed (feed)
segments.commentary: Revenue +25.9% YoY; EBITDA margin 10.5%, with raw material price increases still outpacing selling price increases, though corrections are underway.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected to return to 7-8% in the current year, subject to about one month to pass through price hikes; management says it is not a structural reset.
Consolidated guidance unchanged: 10% volume growth and 15% revenue growth for FY27; India volume growth targeted at 8-10%.

Additional milk price correction of about 2-2.5% in the ongoing quarter, on top of about 1.4% in Dodla standalone and about 4% in Africa over the past year; VAP and ghee corrections were larger (INR3-4/kg VAP, per call).
Procurement cost expected to normalise from Q2 FY27; no bulk SMP/butter sales expected this year as the company turns a net buyer of commodities.
Africa and Orgafeed EBITDA and volume targets described as achievable; Africa margins typically stronger in Q1 and Q4.
capex_capacity: Maharashtra greenfield project progressing to plan; commercial operations timeline intact.
Total capex programme INR590 crore, funded from cash and internal accruals; no debt drawn.
Under review: capital allocation between the BIADA land in Chandel (Bihar) and additional capacity at the Chandel plant, after due diligence; possible shift of flavoured milk production there.
Board approved INR11.65 crore primary investment for about 2% stake in Sids Farm Pvt Ltd (premium D2C dairy brand), described as a learning investment.
No major ice cream capex planned; ice cream revenue rose from INR16 crore to INR22 crore YoY with spare capacity available.
demand_pricing: Price gap to cooperatives: more than INR10/litre in Tamil Nadu, INR6-7/litre in Karnataka; Amul and Mother Dairy have raised prices; management expects southern cooperatives to follow.
Management is not expanding in Andhra Pradesh, where competitive pricing has risen; focus is on Maharashtra, Karnataka and Bihar.
Consolidated milk realisation INR61.78/litre vs INR62.78 last year (INR59.82 excluding bulk last year); VAP consolidated realisation INR64.11 vs INR61.32.
Packing material cost up 48% YoY, rising to 5.6% of revenue from 4.4%.
Stand-alone VAP (excluding bulk) rose from INR245 crore to INR332 crore YoY (about +36%); FY26 fermented VAP INR842 crore vs INR769 crore prior year.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins stay structurally reset lower, and what are the near-term and mid-term triggers for margin recovery over 6-9 months and 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 7-8% EBITDA margin for the current year, subject to about one month to pass through price hikes. It called the compression seasonal rather than structural and expects similar margins over 2-3 years, helped by Maharashtra procurement and OSAM improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Why take only a roughly 2% stake in Sids Farm, and what is the rationale?
qa_highlights.answer: Described as a learning investment to watch premium D2C dairy consumption patterns, with the option to scale up if the brand shows good trajectory.

qa_highlights.question: Is adjusted procurement growth ex-OSAM of about 5.3% driven mainly by Maharashtra, with other geographies flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Procurement breakup: standalone 17.23 lakh L/day (+3%), overseas 2.52 lakh (+28.5%), OSAM 1.39 lakh. Growth came mostly from Africa, then Maharashtra; other states were maintained, not degrown, given summer months.

qa_highlights.question: Has the worst of margin pressure passed, and is the goodwill and intangibles build-up (about INR250 crore) a write-off risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the worst to be behind on procurement cost, with marginal corrections possible. OSAM carries about INR100 crore goodwill and about INR150 crore branding, amortised on standard fair value; no impairment or write-off is expected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the company's stance on ice cream capacity and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: No major ice cream capex planned. Ice cream revenue rose from INR16 crore to INR22 crore, with spare capacity; decisions deferred until the current year plays out.

qa_highlights.question: How much incremental price hike has been taken, and what is the volume outlook after the hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Average price increase of about 2% consolidated: Dodla about 1.4%, Africa about 4%. A further 2-2.5% correction on milk is planned in the ongoing quarter, implying 4-5% for the year. Volume guidance of 8-10% for India was unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the price gap to cooperatives and are competitors likely to raise prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Gap is more than INR10/litre in Tamil Nadu and INR6-7/litre in Karnataka. Amul and Mother Dairy have raised prices, and management expects southern cooperatives to follow due to delayed farmer payments.

qa_highlights.question: What are the procurement cost and realisation figures for June and July, and the consolidated realisation split?
qa_highlights.answer: Procurement cost held at about INR41.2-41.3/litre across May to July. Consolidated milk realisation INR61.78 vs INR62.78 last year (INR59.82 ex-bulk last year); VAP consolidated realisation INR64.11 vs INR61.32. Africa realisation about INR65 vs about INR58-59 a year ago.

qa_highlights.question: Will bulk SMP and butter sales return this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Not expected this year; the company will be a net buyer of commodities because the flush-season volume surge did not occur. Curd sales were INR333.96 crore for the quarter; FY26 fermented VAP was INR842 crore vs INR769 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Africa and Orgafeed targets and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Kenya at about 80% utilisation (1.5 lakh L installed, about 1.1 lakh L in use); Uganda at full capacity with a greenfield under consideration. Africa and feed EBITDA and volume targets described as achievable; Africa margins are typically stronger in Q1 and Q4.

risks_watch: Procurement cost normalisation from Q2 FY27 depends on El Nino-linked supply tightness, lower inventory and monsoon timing; management says there is no assured decline.
Pass-through lag of about one month on the 2-2.5% milk correction; the 7-8% EBITDA margin recovery depends on it.
Price gap to cooperatives above INR10/litre in Tamil Nadu and INR6-7/litre in Karnataka limits market share gains in core southern markets; Andhra Pradesh expansion on hold.
Milk sales volume growth slowed to about 14.5% YoY in standalone with Africa milk volume up about 33%; the company has not split standalone and Africa volume growth clearly.
Net buyer status and no bulk sales this year reduce the earnings buffer; packing material cost up 48% YoY to 5.6% of revenue.
Monitor Maharashtra greenfield commercial timelines, the BIADA Chandel land versus capacity capital allocation decision, the INR590 crore capex funding from accruals, and OSAM margin improvement.
key_quotes: we are still confident that we will maintain between the 7% and 8% EBITDA margins, even in the current year that we are at
These are mostly seasonal corrections and not structural in nature.
So, I don't see, there will be always a pressure because I don't say there won't be any pressure.
I think this year, there won't be enough quantity of bulk sales, we will have to be net buyers of commodity required
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term 7-8% EBITDA margin recovery and on volume guidance, but cautious on the near term, acknowledging procurement costs stayed elevated and price pass-through lagged. Several answers were evasive or deferred on specifics, such as the Chandel capital allocation, the Sids Farm rationale, and ice cream capacity decisions.
